Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health Systems third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as that will cause background noise. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health Systems' financial results for the third quarter. Joining me on the call are Dr. James Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. James Reynolds.

Dr. James Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency across our 52 acute care hospitals and extensive outpatient facilities spanning 14 states.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and year, our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year, the breakdown of revenue by service line, total admissions and patient days year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, and capital expenditure guidance for the next quarter and year.

On same-facility metrics, we saw strong year-over-year admissions growth accelerating into the quarter, with patient days even more robust due to acuity shifts. Total volumes also advanced solidly, supporting our revenue momentum. Service line performance highlighted outpatient acceleration, and we're guiding conservatively yet confidently ahead while maintaining disciplined capex.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Michael to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Reynolds. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Reynolds mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $3.2 billion, an increase of 7.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Let me start by providing a detailed walkthrough of our core volume metrics, beginning with total admissions and patient days, which continue to reflect the resilience of our hospital network amid a dynamic healthcare landscape. These are foundational KPIs directly influencing revenue per admission, case mix index, or CMI, and overall capacity utilization. For the third quarter, ended September 30th, we delivered total admissions of 118,500, up 4.2% year-over-year from 113,700, and up 1.8% quarter-over-quarter from 116,400 in the second quarter. On patient days, we achieved 742,000 days, reflecting a 3.8% year-over-year increase from 714,800 and a 1.2% quarter-over-quarter gain from 733,000. These figures translate to an average length of stay, or ALOS, of 6.26 days—stable quarter-over-quarter but up 10 basis points year-over-year—driven by higher-acuity cases. Our average daily census rose to 8,022 beds, up from 7,910 year-over-year, representing 68% occupancy across our 52 acute care facilities, in line with peers like HCA Healthcare and Universal Health Services.

Inpatient admissions grew 5.1% year-over-year, outpacing observation stays up 2.7%, though pressured by payer scrutiny under Medicare's Two-Midnight Rule. Surgical volumes stood out with 28,400 cases—up 6.8% year-over-year—fueled by rebounding electives like orthopedics and cardiology, now at 95% of pre-COVID levels. Patient days benefited from a 2.5% lift in our CMI to 1.68, reflecting shifts to higher-weighted DRGs such as complex vascular interventions and oncology protocols. Quarter-over-quarter, admissions were led by a 3.1% increase in medical admissions, offset slightly by a 1.2% dip in behavioral health from targeted discharges under value-based arrangements with payers like UnitedHealthcare and Anthem.

Regionally, our Southeast core market with 65% of beds, including Florida and Texas flagships, saw admissions up 6.1% year-over-year and patient days up 5.4%, driven by population in-migration and 42% commercial payer mix. Florida contributed 22% of third-quarter admissions, up 8.2%, benefiting from tourism recovery and Blue Cross Blue Shield bundled ortho payments. Midwest and Northeast clusters were flatter in urban areas like Chicago due to staffing and ASC competition, while rural Kansas and Ohio sites grew patient days 3.5% via tele-ICU expansions.

Trends tie to post-pandemic elective normalization, with labor tightness—nurse turnover at 14% industry-wide—capping upside by 1-2 points. Payer mix held at 55% government, 42% commercial, 3% self-pay/managed Medicaid, with commercial driving 60% of the admissions delta. We've leveraged $150 million in Epic MyChart upgrades for 12% throughput improvement at 15 hospitals via better bed turnover and virtual nursing. Our AI-powered predictive analytics has cut readmissions 8% year-over-year, preserving days while boosting CMS quality scores. Da Vinci Xi rollouts to 12 more ORs boosted surgical admissions 15% in those sites, targeting CMI to 1.72 by year-end. Outpatient shifts via ASC divestitures trimmed low-acuity days 2%, countered by our Hospital at Home program in five markets.

Looking forward, we see Q4 admissions growth of 4-5% year-over-year, patient days 3-4%, assuming normal flu ramp and no COVID resurgence. Risks like CMS IPPS cuts proposed at -2.9% for FY2024 are noted, but our 92% vaccination rate and wage premiums position us well, with upside from Sunbelt expansions and risk-sharing contracts.

Building on that, let's dive into same-facility admissions and patient days growth, both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter. These metrics are core to our hospital segment, about 85% of consolidated revenues, underscoring resilience across our 120-hospital footprint amid payer shifts and workforce constraints. Same-facility admissions, excluding six de novo facilities since Q3 2023 and three Midwest divestitures, delivered 2.8% year-over-year growth, accelerating from 1.9% in Q2—our strongest since 2019 pre-pandemic. Quarter-over-quarter, admissions grew 1.4% from Q2, defying summer softness.

Patient days grew more robustly at 3.6% year-over-year, up from 2.7% prior quarter, driven by ALOS up to 4.7 days from 4.5. Quarter-over-quarter, patient days expanded 2.1%, with 68% network-wide occupancy versus 65% in Q2 and peer average of 64% per Definitive Healthcare. Year-over-year admissions were broad-based, led by 5.2% in high-acuity cardiovascular like PCI and TAVR, from $150 million hybrid OR investments at 25 facilities, aligning with ACC NCDR 4-6% industry uptick. Orthopedics grew 3.9% via Stryker Mako in 40% of joints programs, lifting CMI to 1.68 from 1.62. General medicine moderated to 1.2% as ASCs ramped 12%. Patient days outpaced via 1.1-day ALOS lift from oncology CAR-T and neuro stroke cases up 7%.

Regionally, Southeast 45 facilities from Florida to Carolinas led at 4.1% admissions, with 42% Medicare Advantage versus 38% national CMS average, plus Florida post-Hurricane tailwinds. Southwest Texas/Arizona at 3.2%, aided by Philips tele-ICU cutting diversions 15%. Northeast urban like New York/Philly at 0.9% faced nurse mandates and competition from Northwell/Penn, countered by $20 million travel nurse cuts via internal float pool and Qventus AI scheduling.

Quarter-over-quarter reflected seasonality reversal, with 2.5% surgical ramp in bariatrics/spines, 0.2-day ALOS extension from pneumonia/trauma, lifting ADC to 1,850 from 1,810. Epic EMR at 90% facilities slashed discharge delays 22% via bed dashboards. Payer rate hikes with UnitedHealthcare/Humana at 4.5% on commercial boosted referrals. CMS Enhancing Oncology Model covered 15,000 days, yielding 3% better outcomes.

This validates our High-Acuity, High-Efficiency playbook, prioritizing complex care with CMI accretion, disciplined 4.5% capex on 10 new ICUs in Dallas-Fort Worth/Phoenix. We expect Q4 same-facility admissions 2.5-3.5% year-over-year, patient days 3.0-4.0%, matching HCA/UHS but with 150bps occupancy edge. Paired with 3.2% net revenue per admission, hospital EBITDA margins hit 22.1%, up 110bps.

Next, our revenue breakdown by service line totaled $3.2 billion for the quarter, up 8.2% year-over-year same-facility. This reflects pivot to high-margin outpatient/ambulatory, inpatient resilience despite respiratory pressures, and payer mix discipline. Using net patient revenue per case-adjusted admission, payer-adjusted per-visit, and service line CMI for comparability.

Inpatient acute care: 52% or $1.66 billion, +4.1% year-over-year. Adjusted admissions up 2.8% to 185,000, CMI to 1.95 from 1.2-point expansion on complex cardio/sepsis. Revenue per admission +1.3% to $8,020, Medicare 48%, commercial 38%, Medicaid 14%, bolstered by IPPS. Sunbelt Texas/Florida/Arizona grew 6% on demographics/electives; Rust Belt Ohio/Pennsylvania 1-2% headwinds from Medicaid unwind. Epic/Cerner AI cut ALOS 0.3 days to 4.7, improving turnover 5%.

Outpatient/ambulatory: 28% or $896 million, +14.7%. 12% volume to 2.1 million encounters, per-visit +2.4% to $380. HOPDs/observation 55% ($493 million) from OPPS cardio caths; ASCs/freestanding ERs 30% ($269 million), 35 ASCs like Tenet de novos, high-ASP endoscopy/joints/pain up 18%, margins to 32%; imaging/diagnostics 15% ($134 million) via 4D CT/RadNet. Southeast 17% growth on Florida Boomers/35% MA; $150 million for 10 new ASCs targeting 20% EBITDA like Surgery Partners; Amwell telehealth +25% quarter-over-quarter, 15% visits.

Physician/professional: 12% or $384 million, +9.5%. wRVU +7% to 2.8 million: primary 40%, oncology 30%, hospitalists 30%. Per wRVU +2.2% to $68 via MIPS/value-based 25% lives like Optum. Turnover to 8%; Dallas-Fort Worth 60% growth, rural Tennessee FQHCs.

Post-acute/other: 8% or $256 million, +6.8%. Behavioral 45% ($115 million, +10% IOP/PHP); home health 30% ($77 million, LHC JV); labs/pharma 25% ($64 million, $45 million 340B). Margins +150bps to 18%.

Mix shifted 200bps to outpatient/professional versus last year, aligning CMS site-neutral/2.2% FY2025 IPPS inflation. Payer: Medicare 46%, commercial 37%, managed Medicaid 14%, other 3%. Labor +5.2% offset by 3% optimization/Vizient. Forward, $500 million tuck-in M&A for ASCs in Phoenix/Nashville to 30% outpatient by 2026; Nuance/PathAI for $100 million savings. Q4 service line growth 7-9%, full-year $11.4-11.6 billion.

Our operating expenses were $2.68 billion, representing 83.75% of net revenue. We continue focusing on cost management while investing in growth, particularly supply chain resilience. Net income was $285 million, or $2.05 per share. We're pleased and confident in annual goals.

Turning to guidance, for same-facility volume and revenue growth: excluding recent Midwest divestitures and two Texas/Arizona greenfields, we're guiding Q4 2024 same-facility revenue growth 4.5-5.5%, FY2025 4.0-5.0%. This builds on Q3's 4.2%, from high-acuity commercial/outpatient. Admissions 2.0-3.0% Q4, 1.5-2.5% FY2025; revenue per admission +2.5-3.0% both. Outpatient 58% mix up from 52% three years ago, 5.0-6.0% Q4, 4.5-5.5% FY2025 via ASCs/procedure rooms like Tenet USPI.

Inpatient adjusted admissions 2.5-3.5% Q4 on flu/RSV medical offset ortho/cardio pull-forward; patient days 2.0-3.0%, ALOS 4.6 days via Horizon Flow Qventus AI, discharge delays -15%. Outpatient encounters 5.5-6.5% Q4, ASCs +12%, revenue per low-double-digits on CY2025 Medicare PFS site-neutral/3-5% payer uplifts UnitedHealthcare/Anthem quality-tied.

Revenue per admission +2.5-3.0% Q4, 2.0-2.5% FY2025; mix commercial 52%, Medicare 28%, Medicaid 15%, other 5%; commercial +4-5%, MA denial <8% via ClaimBridge AI like CHS. Sunbelt Florida/Texas/Georgia 45% beds: 6.0-7.0% Q4 revenue, admissions +4% on demographics/tourism/88% occupancy Miami-Dade da Vinci 2,500 procedures/CMI +15%. Northeast/Midwest 35% beds 2.0-3.0%, softer electives/12% denials mitigated travel nurses to 5%/local schools like UHS.

$250 million FY2025 capex 40% digital: Epic MyChart 80% by Q1 +25% self-scheduling/no-shows 12%; telehealth Zoom/TytoCare 18% primary/ED shift to IRBs/LTACHs; RPA Thoughtful AI A/R 45 days +50bps margins. Neuroscience 60 hospitals +8% Q3 guide 7-9% FY2025 Edwards TAVR +20%; behavioral +500 beds opioid 10% revenue; 70% commercial renew Q1 +4% STAR >4.2. Risks labor 3.5%/RN CA shortages/MA clawbacks 200bps shift; upside electives/flu +50-100bps.

On capex specifically, we're guiding $275 million Q4 2024, up from Q3 $240 million, FY2025 $1.35-1.45 billion, 12-15% over FY2024 $1.2 billion, 4.8% of $29 billion revenue. Historical $3.5 billion past three years 12-15% IRR, below 5.2% peer median.

Facilities/de novos 45% FY2025 ~$650 million: Q4 $150 million three Sunbelt ASCs Texas/Florida +12 ORs ortho/GI 25-30% margins; FY2025 $200 million five more/micro-hospitals Phoenix/Charlotte, Sunbelt 60%/Northeast $100 million seismic/behavioral. Equipment/tech 30% ~$420 million: Q4 $80 million Siemens/GE MRIs/CTs +20-25% throughput Nuance AI; FY2025 $150 million 15 da Vinci Xi +15% MIS like Tenet CMI +0.3. IT/digital 20% ~$280 million: Q4 $60 million Epic Hyperdrive FHIR 90%; FY2025 $100 million telehealth/Zoom ambient AI 2 million visits/Palo Alto cyber. Maintenance 5% ~$70 million HVAC/Joint Commission/ESG.

Supports 5-7% revenue CAGR to 2027, 3-5 year paybacks, 70% ops FCF $900 million/30% revolver SOFR+150. Risks CMS OPPS -2.7%/labor; Turner pre-negotiate. ROIC to 11% FY2026 > UHS 9.5%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Heart Failure Management Program has shown promising results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, which now handles 18% of primary care visits and has boosted retention by integrating remote diagnostics.

Following that, Robert will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including supply chain optimization through our GPO with HealthTrust, yielding 4-5% non-labor savings, and staffing model improvements via CareSync predictive analytics, realizing $150 million annualized productivity gains with RN turnover down to 12%. These have resulted in significant cost savings, including 15% on ortho implants and agency spend capped at 8%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Robert. We are committed to driving innovation across our organization. We are investing in new technologies and partnerships to improve patient care, enhance efficiency, and create new revenue streams. Our current projects include AI-driven diagnostics with Nuance and PathAI for pathology, and telemedicine expansion with Zoom and TytoCare, which directly address rising operational costs and access gaps while adding ancillary revenue.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Reynolds.

Dr. James Reynolds:
Thank you, Elena. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from David Lerner with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lerner:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of supply chain optimization?

Robert Kline:
Sure, David. Our supply chain optimization via HealthTrust GPO has delivered 4-5% reductions in non-labor expenses, including 15% savings on high-cost ortho implants for total knee replacements, per Vizient benchmarks. Amid 6-8% pharmaceutical inflation, bulk procurement and vendor consolidation have protected margins, particularly in Sunbelt markets where volumes are highest.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Great question, Emily. Our telehealth platform, integrated with Amwell and TytoCare, is scaling to 2 million encounters annually, capturing 18% of primary care and diverting 20% of ED visits to virtual care, preserving inpatient capacity. This has added $80 million in ancillary revenue, improved retention 18%, and enhanced access in rural areas, with revenue growth in the low-double-digits from virtual urgent care and follow-ups.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Ruiz with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Ruiz:
Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Elena Vasquez:
Absolutely, Mark. Our $420 million FY2025 tech capex includes da Vinci Xi expansions for 15% MIS growth, Epic Hyperdrive for FHIR interoperability reducing denials 18%, and AI like Nuance Dragon for documentation savings of $100 million annualized. Partnerships with Edwards Lifesciences for TAVR and Tempus for NGS oncology enhance MSK CCSP reimbursements to $45,000 per episode, targeting CMI uplift and 7-9% neuroscience volumes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sophia Lee:
Thanks. On the strategic priorities, how do you see portfolio optimization playing out with M&A?

Michael Chen:
Hi Sophia. Portfolio optimization remains key, with our $1.2 billion Coastal Health acquisition adding 1,200 beds at 15% EBITDA tuck-in. We're eyeing $5-10 billion tuck-ins in Southeast/Arizona with strong Medicaid supplements, plus two Dallas micro-hospitals. This supports 6-8% FY2025 revenue growth, funded by $1.4-1.6 billion FCF.

Dr. James Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health Systems third quarter Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
